name: DeltaBreen Analytics
author: deltabreen

sections.description:
DeltaBreen Analytics puts Analytics by DeltaBreen on your site: one small script that counts your traffic, draws heatmaps, records sessions and runs A/B tests, without a cookie. Paste your site key, and the numbers arrive within a minute.

What you see

  • Traffic: visitors, visits, pages, where people came from (search, social, email, campaigns with their UTM tags), countries, devices and browsers, live as it happens.
  • Heatmaps: where people click and how far they scroll on each page, at each screen width.
  • Session recordings: watch a visit as it happened, with every form field masked before it leaves the visitor’s browser.
  • A/B tests and feature flags: test a headline or a page in the visual editor or in your theme’s code, with results that are safe to check at any time.
  • Goals and funnels: sign-ups, orders and any event you choose, and where people drop out on the way.
  • Web Vitals and errors: how fast pages load for real visitors, and the JavaScript errors they meet.
  • Surveys: a short question on the pages you choose.

Private by design

  • No cookie, so no banner is needed for it. A visitor is a daily changing, anonymous id until your site asks and they agree.
  • Follows the WP Consent API. With a consent plugin that speaks it, a visitor’s yes to statistics keeps their visits together across days, and a no turns that off at once. A banner built on the IAB framework (TCF v2) can be followed instead.
  • IP addresses are never stored, and the data is kept in the EU.
  • Page caches are safe. Every page is the same for every visitor: consent is read in the visitor’s browser, and a signed-in user is asked for from your own site with an answer no cache keeps.

WooCommerce

Each order is counted once as a Purchase, with its total and currency as revenue, so your channels, campaigns, pages and A/B tests show the money they bring. A failed order is not counted, and opening the order page again counts nothing. Works with WooCommerce’s order tables (HPOS).

Signed-in customers

Signed-in users can be known by their WordPress user id, so their visits on a phone and a laptop count as one person. With your site’s identity secret, Analytics knows the id came from your site and not from someone typing in a browser’s console.

Light on your pages

The tracker is about 5 KB, loads after your page and never holds it up. Recordings, heatmaps and the visual editor load only on the pages that need them. Speed plugins (WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, Autoptimize, SiteGround Optimizer, Jetpack Boost, Cloudflare Rocket Loader) are told to leave it alone, so no visit is lost to a delayed script.

Plans

Free counts 10,000 events a month on one site, with 300 recordings, three heatmap pages and one running test, and keeps a year of history. Paid plans are one flat price for your whole team: you are never charged for going over, and a paid plan keeps counting past its allowance. See pricing.

Getting started

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open Analytics and sign in with your email (a new account starts on Free), then add your site.
  3. Copy the site key from Sites → your site → Install, and paste it in Settings → DeltaBreen Analytics.
  4. Open your site in a private window: the visit shows in Analytics within a minute.

External services

This plugin connects your site to Analytics by DeltaBreen, a web analytics service run by DeltaBreen. It does nothing until you paste a site key, and the plugin’s own PHP never calls the service: the calls below are made by your visitors’ browsers.

  • The tracker script. On each page, the visitor’s browser loads your site’s script from https://dbreencdn.eu/s/<your site key>.js (or from the path of your own site you put in “Loaded from”). Recordings, heatmaps, surveys and the visual editor load further parts from the same address, only on pages that use them.
  • What the script sends, and when. While a page is open, the browser sends to https://dbreencdn.eu the page’s address (with query values that look personal left out), the page it came from, the screen’s width, clicks and scrolling for heatmaps, load times, JavaScript errors, the events your site sends, a recording of the visit when recordings are switched on for the site (with every form field masked), and answers to your surveys. With the visitor’s consent, it also stores an id in their browser’s local storage. For a signed-in user, when “Know signed-in users” is on, it sends their WordPress user id and, with the identity secret, a token that proves it. On a WooCommerce order’s page, it sends the order’s total, currency and number of items.
  • What the service does with it. The visitor’s IP address is read to find their country and to make the day’s anonymous id, then dropped; it is never stored. Browsers that send Global Privacy Control are counted but never recorded.

Analytics by DeltaBreen’s terms of service and privacy policy.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins → Add New, search for DeltaBreen Analytics, then Install and Activate.
  2. Go to Settings → DeltaBreen Analytics and paste your site key (it starts with ans_).
  3. Optionally paste the identity secret from Sites → your site → Settings, so signed-in users are verified.
sections.faq:
Do I need a cookie banner for this?

Not for Analytics: it sets no cookie and stores nothing on the visitor’s device until they consent, and it never stores an IP address. If your site has a banner anyway, a consent plugin that follows the WP Consent API is followed by itself. Your privacy notice should still say that you use Analytics by DeltaBreen.

Why don’t I see my own visits?

Administrators are not counted, so your own clicks don’t fill your numbers. Open the site in a private window, or untick “Do not count administrators”.

Does it count a staging copy of my site?

No. A copy WordPress names staging, development or local sends nothing, unless you tick “Count every copy”. Analytics only takes the hostnames you list for your site anyway.

Can I load it from my own domain?

Yes. Send a path of your site, such as /stats, on to our collector at your server or CDN, put that path in “Loaded from”, and switch on Settings → Site → Behind my own proxy in Analytics. Content blockers then don’t cut your numbers. The proxy guide has nginx and Cloudflare Worker recipes.

How do I send my own events?

Call dba('track', 'Newsletter signup') from your theme’s or a plugin’s JavaScript, with properties as a second argument if you like. The tracker guide lists everything it can do.

Which visitors are left out of A/B tests?

Only visitors who consented, or who are signed in, take part, so each sees the same variant every time; everyone else sees your page as it is.
sections.changelog:
1.0.1

  • When the tracker loads through a path of your own site and your site cannot reach its own address to check that path, the settings page says the path could not be checked, where it said nothing was counted.

1.0.0

  • First version in the WordPress.org plugin directory. Nothing changes on your site from 0.2.0.

0.2.0

  • Renamed DeltaBreen Analytics, from Analytics by DeltaBreen.
  • Page caches are safe: a signed-in user is asked for from your site in the visitor’s browser, never printed in the page, and consent is read in the browser from the WP Consent API.
  • The tracker loads with WordPress’s own script loading, and speed plugins are told to leave it alone.
  • A staging, development or local copy of the site sends nothing, unless you tick “Count every copy”.
  • The identity secret is never shown again once saved.
  • Follows a consent banner built on the IAB framework (TCF v2) when you tick it.
  • Loads through a path of your own site with its data sent back the same way.
  • Every word can be translated.
  • Works on PHP 7.4 and later.

0.1.1

  • A WooCommerce order is counted once, even when its thank-you page is opened again; failed orders are not counted.
  • Declares compatibility with WooCommerce’s order tables (HPOS) and registers with the WP Consent API.
  • Uninstalling removes the plugin’s settings.
